report.what_happened: Ocrelizumab 300 mg/10 mL was administered on 30 July 2025 and billed to Blue Harbor Health on the medical track, with a drug line of 13500000 cents and an infusion line of 15000 cents [[raw:79]]. The submission was accepted for processing on 31 July 2025 [[raw:80]]. On the 340B side, the TPA qualified the episode on 4 August 2025 [[raw:170]] and requested a rebate from Sagepoint on 8 August 2025 [[raw:172]]. On 30 August 2025 the payer denied the claim as not medically necessary — status code 4, a CO-50 adjustment of 13500000 cents against the drug line — and paid nothing at the claim level, while its own infusion line shows 15000 cents paid [[raw:137]]. Sagepoint approved the $33,750.00 rebate on 10 September 2025 [[raw:184]], and that cash was matched and allocated on 26 September 2025 [[event:8]].
report.why_it_is_open: Reimbursement is denied with no later activity recorded [[verdict:B-10]]: expected $84,240.00, received $0.00 [[calc:reimbursement.expected_usd]] [[calc:reimbursement.received_usd]]. The rebate track closed approved, paid, cash matched [[verdict:C-08]] at $33,750.00 [[calc:rebate.received_usd]]. Cross-track flag X-1 fires because a manufacturer paid a rebate on a claim the payer refused as not medically necessary; that contradiction holds the episode in EXCEPTION.
report.what_i_could_not_determine: The submitted claim carried no 340B flag [[raw:79]], yet a full 340B track qualified and paid — the flag and the track disagree. The remittance also contradicts itself: claim-level payment is $0.00 [[calc:reimbursement.received_usd]], but its infusion line shows 15000 cents paid [[raw:137]], and that 15000 cents is unexplained.
report.what_a_human_should_check_first:
1. Whether the remittance's $0.00 claim total or its 15000-cent infusion line is the accurate record.
2. Why a submission with no 340B flag carried a full, paid rebate track.
3. Whether Sagepoint's rebate approval calls the payer's not-medically-necessary denial into question.
